title: Order an Idea into Steps
subtitle: Turn your creative ideas into clear, workable plans!
objectives: Identify the correct order for a series of steps in a plan.
Recognize when a step is missing or impossible to complete.
Adjust a plan to fit available materials and ensure it is realistic.

scenes.title: Ready for Action!
scenes.narration: Have a brilliant idea but unsure how to start? We'll learn to break big ideas into practical steps. Make plans ready for action!
scenes.visualAction: A child character stands in front of a blank table, looking thoughtful. A lightbulb appears above their head, then fades. Three imaginary drawings float into view briefly.

scenes.title: Steps to Success
scenes.narration: Planning involves more than just listing steps. Order them correctly, check for missing parts, and ensure every step is possible. Good plans lead to success!
scenes.visualAction: A checklist appears with three items: 'Order?', 'Missing?', 'Possible?'. A hand icon points to each item as it's mentioned.

scenes.title: Art Display Challenge
scenes.narration: Imagine displaying three drawings. Here is a plan someone made. Let's examine it closely. Does it make sense? We'll use paper and reusable clips.
scenes.visualAction: Three cartoon drawings appear on screen. A table slides in. A list of jumbled steps appears next to the table.

scenes.title: Spot the Problem
scenes.narration: The plan says 'Attach clips' before 'Choose drawings'. Can you clip drawings not yet picked? No! It also misses checking work. We must fix this!
scenes.visualAction: The jumbled list from the previous scene highlights the 'Attach clips' step, then the 'Choose drawings' step, showing them out of order. A question mark appears over the list.

scenes.title: Build a Better Plan
scenes.narration: First, choose drawings. Then, label them. Arrange them on the table. Only then, attach clips. Finally, check everything. This order makes sense!
scenes.visualAction: The jumbled list transforms into the correct sequence of steps. Each step animates as it's narrated: 1. Choose drawings. 2. Label each. 3. Arrange on table. 4. Attach clips (if needed). 5. Check labels and stability.

scenes.title: Repair the display plan
scenes.narration: Now try the display plan yourself. Reorder its steps, add the missing final check, and explain why choosing drawings must come before attaching clips.
scenes.visualAction: A jumbled paper-display checklist appears; a blank final-check card slides beside it.

scenes.title: Master Planner!
scenes.narration: Great job! You learned to review plans, check order, spot missing steps, and ensure possibility. This skill helps with projects and tasks. Plan smart!
scenes.visualAction: The child character gives a thumbs-up. A thought bubble shows a successful art display. Confetti falls.

reading.title: Why Plan Steps?
reading.text: Planning steps helps you reach your goal smoothly. It's like building with blocks; you need to put them in the right order. If steps are out of place, or if you try to do something impossible, your project might get stuck. Always check if a step is realistic with your available materials.

reading.title: A Good Plan vs. A Tricky Plan
reading.text: A good plan for making a sandwich: 1. Get bread. 2. Add filling. 3. Cut. A tricky plan: 1. Cut bread. 2. Get filling. 3. Add filling. You can't cut bread before you get it! And you need to get the filling before you add it. Order matters!

reading.title: Three Checks for Any Plan
reading.text: Before you start, ask yourself these three questions: 1. Is the order correct? Does one step need to happen before another? 2. Are there any missing steps? Did I forget something important? 3. Is every step possible? Do I have the materials and skills needed for each part?

materials.title: Invented display plan
materials.text: Plan a display of 3 invented drawings: a flower, a boat and a moon. Available materials: paper and reusable clips. Proposed plan: 1) Attach clips to the sheets. 2) Choose the drawings. 3) Arrange them on the table. 4) Add a name label to each. The plan omits a final check of labels and stability.

promptExamples.improved: Give me steps to display three invented drawings using paper and reusable clips. Include choosing, labelling, arranging and a final check.
promptExamples.followup: Move choosing before attaching, and add a check of labels and stability.

activity.title: Repair the order
activity.instructions: Reorder the steps, add the final check and explain why choosing comes before attaching. This is a written planning exercise; you do not need to build a display.
activity.starter: Plan a display of 3 invented drawings: a flower, a boat and a moon. Available materials: paper and reusable clips. Proposed plan: 1) Attach clips to the sheets. 2) Choose the drawings. 3) Arrange them on the table. 4) Add a name label to each. The plan omits a final check of labels and stability.
activity.expectedEvidence: A corrected order, final check, and explanation.

quiz.question: A step needs equipment you do not have. What should you do?
options: Revise the step to work with available materials.
Follow the step without reviewing it.
quiz.explanation: Check whether the plan is feasible and revise it to fit the available materials.

quiz.question: Which order makes sense?
options: Attach clips to the drawings, then choose them.
Choose the drawings, then attach clips if needed.
Do both steps without identifying the drawings.
quiz.explanation: You need to know which drawings you will display before attaching them.

quiz.question: The plan ends with arranging the drawings but has no final check. What should you add?
options: Change the drawing names at random.
Add more clips for no reason.
quiz.explanation: A final check helps you spot a wrong label or a sheet that needs adjusting.

mission.title: A matching game with 6 ready-made cards
mission.instructions: You have 6 ready-made paper cards and a pencil. Write a 5-step plan: draw 3 pairs of symbols, check that every symbol has a matching partner, mix the cards, lay them face down, and begin finding pairs. Put these steps in order and explain why checking comes before mixing. No cutting or extra equipment is needed.
rubric: Cards are laid face down before play.
The plan uses only the supplied cards and pencil.

hints.question: Where do I start?
hints.answer: Which drawings will be displayed? Choose them before deciding where to attach clips.

hints.question: What final step is missing?
hints.answer: Check the names and whether the sheets stay in place.

hints.question: How do I assess my plan?
hints.answer: Check the order, missing steps and whether each step works with the supplied materials.

imageBrief.title: From pairs to a game
imageBrief.composition: Top-down independent diagram: six ready-made paper cards and a pencil. Show drawing three symbol pairs, checking pairs, mixing, then laying cards face down. No scissors, display-table drawings or video characters.
imageBrief.altText: Top-down independent diagram: six ready-made paper cards and a pencil. Show drawing three symbol pairs, checking pairs, mixing, then laying cards face down. No scissors, display-table drawings or video characters.

educatorNotes.sampleAnswer: Activity: choose drawings; label them; arrange on the table; attach clips if needed; check labels and stability. Mission: draw matching pairs; check every pair; mix; lay face down; begin matching.
educatorNotes.commonMisconception: Learners might focus only on the main action steps and forget crucial preparatory or checking steps (e.g., 'gather materials,' 'let dry,' 'check work'). They may also struggle with identifying the *most* logical first step, especially when safety or foundational actions are involved.
reviewChecks: Cards are laid face down before play.
The plan uses only the supplied cards and pencil.
educatorNotes.safetyNotes: Written planning using paper, ready-made cards and a pencil; no cutting, heat or food preparation.
